messages.subject: repeated measures ANOVA with cluster variable?
parts:
Hello, I have a dataset (described below, and attached some exemplar data) for which I was unsure how to do the analysis. I asked around and a repeated measures ANOVA was recommended. I'm relatively new to R, statistical analysis and absolutely new to the ez package (which I'm grateful exists!!) so require some much needed guidance!

The experimental design is as follows. I have 20 cells, 10 of each assigned to control and experimental conditions. Each cell produces a variable number of spontaneous events (where each event has characteristics that I wish to analyse) which I have recorded over a arbitrarily decided time frame. Because of the spontaneity, there is a fairly large amount of variation in the number of spontaneous events between cells (both within and between control and experimental condition) over the arbitrarily decided time period (for example, over 10 minutes, there could be 50 or 500 events for 2 given cells). Because of this intracellular variation, there could be undue over- or under-representation of one cell upon the analysis of the event characteristics. And because of this, it was recommended I perform a repeated measures ANOVA with cell ID as a "cluster variable" to deal with this intracellular variation.

After a bit of reading around, I turned to the ez package (as opposed to the aov and anova functions) due to uneven sample sizes (which from what I gather requires a type II test, which ez assumes and the native R functions don't). However, I am now unsure of how to construct the command within R due to my inexperience with statistical nomenclature/general incompetence! As I understand it, the cell ID would be the 'within-subjects' factor and condition (i.e. control or experiment) would be the 'between-subjects' factor. However, something which I don't understand (presumably because I'm mistaken in my previous sentence), is that it asks for the .wid() argument ("object specifying the column in data that contains the variable specifying the case/Ss identiﬁer"). Could anyone please provide some clarification?

Many thanks.

messages.author: cb25d91fd630a4e5
messages.subject: Re: [ez4r] repeated measures ANOVA with cluster variable?
parts:
Since cell_ID is the unit of repeated ("within") measurement, it
should be supplied as the value of the "wid" argument. Values supplied
to the "within" argument should be manipulated variables in the
experiment that are manipulated within each level of wid, of which you
have none. So the code you want is:

my_anova = ezANOVA(
data = example_data1
, dv = .(event_characteristic)
, wid = .(cell_ID)
, between = .(condition)
)
print(my_anova)

Hi Mike, thank you for the reply. It seems so straightforward now...

I attempted the above code on some data in which I in fact only have 9 cells attributed to one of the conditions and 7 the other and it threw up the following errors:

Warning: Data is unbalanced (unequal N per group). Make sure you specified a well-considered value for the type argument to ezANOVA().
Error in `colnames<-`(`*tmp*`, value = c("Effect", "DFn", "DFd", "SSn", :
'names' attribute [8] must be the same length as the vector [7]
Error in ezANOVA_main(data = data, dv = dv, wid = wid, within = within, :
The car::Anova() function used to compute results and assumption tests seems to have failed. Most commonly this is because you have too few subjects relative to the number of cells in the within-Ss design. It is possible that trying the ANOVA again with "type=1" may yield results (but definitely no assumption tests).

For the first warning, I assume type=2 will suffice. I am unsure how to remedy the remaining errors. I've looked at my raw data, and I can't see any missing values.

parts:
The error speaking about car::Anova() is just the default message that
ezANOVA prints when car::Anova() fails because it's the most common
reason why this would happen. In your case, however, the earlier
printed message about colnames seems to suggest that something else is
awry. To help troubleshoot fastest, can you send me a .RData file with
the data object you tried ezANOVA on, plus the code you wrote in your
call to ezANOVA? To create the .RData file, simply run:
save(my_data,file='data_for_mike.RData')

Mike

Ah, this is the bug reported here: https://github.com/mike-lawrence/ez/issues/1

The resolution is to either download the ez-internal.R file linked in
the comments of the link above and source it after loading ez.

Alternatively, you can use the dev version of ez in which this bug has
been fixed. Instructions for using the dev version are on the github
page for ez (https://github.com/mike-lawrence/ez#readme).

Mike

parts:
Brilliant, I followed the latter piece of advice (the link to the fix didn't work for me), installed the latest dev version and it worked a treat; here are the results for the above dataset: 

$ANOVA
     Effect DFn DFd         F         p p<.05        ges
1 condition   1  13 0.3500109 0.5642539       0.02621803

$`Levene's Test for Homogeneity of Variance`
  DFn DFd        SSn      SSd         F         p p<.05
1   1  13 0.03975061 1.070489 0.4827306 0.4994183   


So we surmise there is no significant difference between conditions and if it were significant, the GES tells us it would be a small association. Levene's test shows homogeneity of variance has not been violated, i.e. the variances between control and experiment are the same. Is this a correct interpretation?

messages.author: cb25d91fd630a4e5
messages.subject: Re: [ez4r] repeated measures ANOVA with cluster variable?
parts: Yup, that would be an appropriate set of inferences to draw from the output.
